_comment: NOT an engine profile.
The *.json files directly under profiles/ are ENGINE profiles: each one
is a single engine configuration and is validated against
profiles/schema/profile-v1.2.json by
src/modules/assembly/tests/test_profile_schema.cpp
ProfileSchema.EveryShippedProfileValidatesUnderV12.  That test scans
the profiles/ ROOT directory only, so this file lives in a
subdirectory on purpose: it is a different kind of artifact.
This file is a MAP FROM PROFILE NAME TO CONNECTIVITY DEFAULTS.
It is read by the `connectivity_profile` key on EngineConfig
(src/engine/include/nimrtc/engine/engine.hpp) and describes the
INTENT of a connectivity profile -- not the addresses.
The engine obeys a table written in code
(src/engine/src/engine_connectivity_profile.cpp,
resolve_connectivity_profile()).  This file documents the same table
for hosts and for people reading the tree; the code is the one that
runs.  Keep the two in sync.
The keys of every profile are the same:
stun          -- gather server-reflexive candidates (a STUN server
is configured when the host did not configure one)
turn_tls      -- 'always' | 'when_available' | 'never'
whether TURN/TLS (RFC 6062) is required or merely
preferred
tcp_fallback  -- fall back to TURN/TCP when TURN/UDP does not get
through
A host's explicit STUN / TURN configuration always WINS over these
defaults: a profile only fills in the keys the host left unset.
